findings.reason: without the plan stating that `_restate_time_fence` is applied before the prompt is composed (moved to the `launch_plan` call in `change_lane`), the change as written regresses the deadline restatement on the very path its measure names, and a worker following the text literally would either ship that regression or be blocked on a decision the plan does not settle.
findings.text: §15's Change says "A lane change composes from the prompt with its fence already restated, so the file carries both the restated fence and the named figures", but in `change_lane` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1651`) the plan is composed from the un-restated prompt — `_lane_prompt` at `:1793` returns the record's own prompt (the previous attempt's fence) or a bare advice string, and `launch_plan(prompt=prompt, …)` at `:1824` is handed exactly that; `_restate_time_fence` is applied only at the file write, `:1920`, whose own comment says restating "is what stops the worker reading the first attempt's deadline" — so a worker implementing §15 as written writes the lane-change file from `plan.stdin_text`, which carries the previous attempt's deadline (or, on a continued lane change, no fence at all), and §15's done-when requires that same file to carry "the restated fence"; only `resume_plan` at `:1337` restates before composing

findings.reason: the fallback ("only where the plan carries none") is the part at risk and the measure does not test it, so the plan must assert the codex file still carries the brief (and say what happens to an inherited listing on a move to an argv lane).
findings.text: the clause "the same two-figure node dispatched on codex writes a `prompt.txt` with no figure listing, the paths riding `-i`" cannot fail for the failure it should catch: `launch_plan` returns `stdin_text=""` for a dialect where `stdin_prompt` is false (`reckon/_backends.py:2349`), and the fresh dispatch feeds the worker `open(prompt_path, "rb")` as its stdin (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1589`), so an implementation that writes the file from `plan.stdin_text` without the fallback §15 states produces an empty `prompt.txt` on codex that passes the clause while every codex worker is handed no prompt at all; no other clause in §15 catches it, and the same clause is silent on the lane change of a figure-carrying run onto a lane whose images ride `-i`, where `_lane_prompt` carries the inherited listing forward so the file asserts figures that lane delivers on argv

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every anchor resolves: `prompt_path.write_text(prompt)` is `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2126`; `prompt_path.write_text(_restate_time_fence(prompt, …))` is `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1920`; `_write_resume_prompt` is `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1205`; `IMAGE_MODALITY` `reckon/_backends.py:143`; `_prompt_naming_images` `:2156`; `declares_image_input` `:2141`; `declared_input_modalities` `reckon/flight.py:1953`; and every write path including `tests/test_crew_lane_change.py` exists.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §15's codex clause ("dispatched on codex writes a `prompt.txt` with no figure listing") is satisfied by an empty prompt file, which is what an implementation that writes `plan.stdin_text` unconditionally produces on a non-stdin dialect, since `launch_plan` sets `stdin_text=""` when `dialect.stdin_prompt` is false (`reckon/_backends.py:2349`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §15 puts every log "under the run directory", the durable crew run record, and names no scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols §15 names (`_prompt_naming_images`, `declares_image_input`, `declared_input_modalities`) are named by mechanism, and no stage label, ticket number or version tag enters a path or a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §15's stated mechanism does not produce its own done-when on the lane-change path: the plan `change_lane` builds is composed from the un-restated prompt, so writing the run's prompt file from "the prompt `launch_plan` composed" drops the fence restatement that today's write performs.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15 carries one deliverable, the prompt file a worker reads on every launch path; the IMAGE_MODALITY comment and the one-reader unification attach to the same named-figure mechanism (an earlier review raised this as a second goal and the author declined it with a reason).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §15's `depends-on` names `a-review-can-see-the-figure#s14` (landed, `9656c79ab`) and the plan's `plan-informs` names `scoring-should-stop-a-promotion`, which is the plan §15's reader unification serves.
